claims.text: The as-deposited FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy coating has a typical, unrefined dislocation network.
Cyclic pre-straining can promote dislocation-cell formation in the BCC phase.
Cyclic pre-straining can promote deformation-twin formation in the BCC phase.
The effects of cyclic pre-straining depend on its amplitude and number of cycles.
The pre-strain-induced dislocation cells become hardened internal barriers to further dislocation propagation.
Deformation twins in the BCC phase act as internal barriers to further dislocation propagation.
Cyclic pre-straining reconfigures the dislocation network in the BCC phase.
Continuous dislocation motion is responsible for creep deformation under sustained loading in the coating.
Pre-strain-induced dislocation cells and twins interrupt and retard the dislocation motion responsible for creep.
Optimized cyclic pre-straining improves creep resistance during continuous loading.
Optimally pre-strained coatings will have a lower steady-state creep rate than untreated coatings.
Optimally pre-strained coatings will have a higher yield stress than untreated coatings.
TEM or EBSD will reveal clearly defined dislocation cells in BCC regions after optimized pre-straining.
TEM or EBSD will reveal deformation twins in BCC regions after optimized pre-straining.
The proposed mechanism operates during continuous loading near the creep threshold.
The proposed mechanism operates only within a pre-strain amplitude and cycle-number window that produces beneficial microstructural evolution without deleterious damage.
